sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: license ladder ages, exam triggers, residency proofs, permit terms and restriction codes
Confusable pairs among the Missouri license classes, ages and document rules, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A02
On the license ladder the intermediate Class F license opens at 16, while both the full Class F license and the Class E for-hire license open at 18. [A02]
Why it matters: group license ladder; confusable intermediate versus full versus for-hire ages; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A02
Rider training is mandatory only for the motorcycle instruction permit taken at 15 and a half; an applicant aged 16 or older can get that permit without the course. [A02]
Why it matters: group motorcycle permit; confusable early versus standard age; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A03
A Class M motorcycle license can be held from 16, but a commercial license waits until 18, and its Hazardous Materials or School Bus endorsement until 21. [A03]
Why it matters: group license classes; confusable motorcycle versus commercial ages; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A04
A brand-new applicant takes all four tests, but a newcomer transferring a valid out-of-state license takes just the vision and road sign tests. [A04]
Why it matters: group examination; confusable new license versus transfer; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A04
For a lapsed Missouri license the guide treats six months and 184 days as the same window: beyond it, the full four-part exam applies again. [A04]
Why it matters: group examination; confusable months versus days; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A05
The 90-day age limit applies to official government letters used as residency proof, while utility bills simply have to be current. [A05]
Why it matters: group documents; confusable letter window versus current bills; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A06
The motorcycle permit costs $12.75 or $10.00 depending on the starting age and lasts up to 6 months (182 days), half the 12-month term of the regular instruction permit shown on the same chart. [A06]
Why it matters: group permits; confusable motorcycle versus instruction permit terms; dynamic fee.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A06
A nondriver ID card used only for voting can be issued from age 17 and a half and costs $0.00 on the fee chart. [A06]
Why it matters: group identification; difficulty low; dynamic fee.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A07
Restriction code Q signals more than five restrictions, and code U marks an uncoded restriction whose wording appears on the back of the card when space allows. [A07]
Why it matters: group restriction codes; confusable Q versus U; difficulty high.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A07
A law enforcement officer, a judge or a physician may ask the Department to add a restriction to your license. [A07]
Why it matters: group restrictions; prereq restriction codes; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A01
Moving or operating a farm tractor or farm implement on a highway for agricultural work, even briefly, does not call for a Missouri license. [A01]
Why it matters: group exemptions; continuation of the exemption list in C.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A01
Every permit issued to someone younger than 21 carries a marking that identifies the holder as a minor. [A01]
Why it matters: group minor marking; prereq GDL ladder.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A02
The minor marking also appears on licenses issued before 21; once you turn 21 you may buy a replacement without it or simply use the old one until it expires. [A02]
Why it matters: group minor marking; confusable permit versus license marking.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A03
A motorized bicycle needs no motorcycle endorsement, though its rider must carry a valid operator license or a higher class. [A03]
Why it matters: group license classes; confusable motorized bicycle versus motorcycle.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A03
Renewing a license, nondriver ID or instruction permit can require showing the lawful status, identity, Social Security, name-change and residency proofs again, plus the previous license. [A03]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A04
Someone aged 65 or older renewing a non-REAL ID non-commercial permit, license or nondriver ID may skip the place-of-birth documents. [A04]
Why it matters: group documents; confusable renewal exemption versus REAL ID.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A05
The guide defines a residential address as your true, fixed and permanent principal home, the place you intend to come back to even while living somewhere else for now. [A05]
Why it matters: group residency; glossary residential address.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A05
Without a Social Security number you bring a status letter from the Social Security Administration, except a nonimmigrant foreign student with an F or J classification who is not authorized to work. [A05]
Why it matters: group Social Security; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A05
Applicants who already verified their Social Security number on a current Missouri credential may be allowed to state the number aloud instead of showing a document. [A05]
Why it matters: group Social Security; confusable renewal versus first-time proof.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A05
An application filed without a Social Security number may go to the central office for final approval before the card is printed and mailed. [A05]
Why it matters: group Social Security; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A06
To prove a new last name you can bring a certified marriage license, divorce decree, court order, adoption papers or an amended birth certificate, but a first- or middle-name change is proven only by a certified court order. [A06]
Why it matters: group name change; confusable last versus first or middle name.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A07
Examiners, license clerks, relatives, police officers and the listed health professionals who doubt your medical fitness to drive report it on the Driver Condition Report, Form 4319. [A07]
Why it matters: group medical referral; prereq physician statement rule.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0011]
